conventions: In a verbless poetic line that fronts a prepositional phrase before an indefinite nominal, the construction-supplied copula goes to the preposition under rule 49, not to the nominal standing after it: `מִימִינוֹ אֵשׁ דָּת` -> *At his right hand was a fiery law* (33.2) and `וּמִתַּחַת זְרֹעֹת עוֹלָם` -> *And underneath are the everlasting arms* (33.27) both put the copula on the preposition, and 33.27's compound `מִתַּחַת` is fused and headed on the governing first morpheme under rules 23 and 30. Rule 49's closing adjunct carve-out was read as not reaching these, because the Hebrew writes no definite nominal predicate for the copula to join; the competing reading, which puts *was*/*are* on `דָּת` and `זְרוֹעַ`, is named in both verses' notes. The chapter treats an ordinary prepositional predicate the same way (33.3, 33.8, 33.29) and puts the copula on the nominal wherever the predicate is nominal (33.1, 33.17, 33.20, 33.22, 33.24, 33.25, 33.27, 33.29).

In the repeated blessing formula of 33.13-16 the ablative `מִן` takes the ASV's written *for* (`מִמֶּגֶד` -> *for the precious things*), and `מֶגֶד` takes *the precious things* headed on *precious*, *things* being the supplied generic under rule 31 and the *the* supplied under rules 15 and 29. `רֹאשׁ הַרְרֵי־קֶדֶם` -> *the chief things of the ancient mountains* (33.15) follows the same division, headed on *chief*, and the `קֶדֶם` and `עוֹלָם` of 33.15 and 33.27 are rendered attributively under rule 28 rather than taking an *of*. The five `מֶגֶד` units and the one `רֹאשׁ` unit are one judgment, so a verse aligned alone from this stretch should not re-decide the head.

`יַחַד` at 33.5 takes only the written *together*, and the *All* standing before *the tribes of Israel* is `added`: no `כֹּל` stands in the clause, the determiner slot before the noun already holds the supplied *the* of rule 29, and *All ... together* cannot be one rendering under rule 30, which wants one English word and contiguity. `יָחְדָּו` at 33.17 instead takes the whole *all of them* headed on *all*, because there the ASV writes no separate adverb for it and the alternative would leave the morpheme unrepresented beside three added tokens. The apparent split between the two verses is the ASV's and not the analysis's. Where a `כֹּל` is present it takes the word written for it, as at 33.3 (*All his saints*) and 33.12 (*all the day long*).
report: Read all 51 candidate lemma groups and the full dump end to end. Every multi-treatment bucket traces to either a different Hebrew construction or a different English rendering the ASV actually wrote, so no cross-verse split was found and patches is empty.

The buckets that looked most like splits, and why each is not one: betach at 33.12 vs 33.28 (a written le takes *in* in one, the bare adverbial accusative takes *in safety* whole in the other, rules 33/40); rosh + am at 33.5 vs 33.21 (only 33.21 writes the italic *with*, given to the adverbial accusative under rule 33); yad at 33.7 vs 33.11 (adverbial accusative *With his hands* vs construct rectum *of his hands*); al + suffix at 33.12 (one takes *by*, the second is silenced because the ASV promotes its object to a bare direct object of *covereth*, rule 40); min at 33.2 vs 33.13-16 (*from* for the theophany, *for* throughout the blessing formula); the two le of 33.10 unrepresented against nine others taking *of* (teach X Y writes a bare indirect object, rule 40).

The two whom of 33.8 are consistent with each other: the written asher takes the first and the resumptive suffix is unrepresented under rule 22, exactly as rule 43's closing sentence rules for asher bo; the second, rewritten at the head of the coordinated clause, is that clause's own resumptive suffix under rule 22's coordinated-clause paragraph.

All seven added units were counted against the morphemes that could license them and each survives. The closest call is *All the tribes of Israel together* at 33.5, where 33.17 gives the whole *all of them* to yachdaw: the two are not a split, because 33.5 writes *together* for its adverb and 33.17 writes no separate adverb at all, and *All ... together* cannot fuse under rule 30 in any case (two English words, non-contiguous), while rule 15's supplied determiner reaches only the slot the phrase's supplied *the* already fills. The chapter's two kol both take the *All*/*all* written for them (33.3, 33.12), so the count is clean. No corpus round was needed.

BSB: all 8 disagreements are documented convention differences, none an error. Four are rule 40 recastings that leave a preposition with no English word (33.4 dative le after *commanded us*, 33.10 twice after *teach*, 33.12 alaw after *covereth him*); one is the resumptive object suffix of 33.8 discussed above; three are the paragogic nun of 33.11 and the paragogic he of 33.16 and 33.23, which rule 32 makes their own unrepresented units and which BSB attaches to the host word.

Three conventions recorded: the copula on a fronted prepositional predicate (33.2, 33.27), the repeated mimmeged formula of 33.13-16, and the yachad/yachdaw pair. No promotion: rule 22's coordinated-clause paragraph, rule 46's closing and rule 49's own adjunct carve-out already decide everything this chapter met, and the one novel judgment — the correlative *as ... so* given whole to the comparative kaf at 33.25 — occurs once, with no corpus precedent shown, which is too thin to bind later chapters.
